questions.knowledge_point: Listing the Elements of a Set Defined Over a Special Set
questions.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined as

$$
A={{n}^{4}:n\in Z}.
$$

Which of the following sets is equivalent to $A?$
questions.worked_solution:
The elements of $A$ are all the terms of the sequence ${a}_{n},$ given by

$$
{a}_{n}={n}^{4},\,n\in Z={0,\pm 1,\pm 2,\pm 3,…}.
$$

Let's write down some terms of our sequence until the pattern becomes clear.

$$
\begin{aligned} & ⋮ \\ {a}_{-3} & =(-3)^{4}=81 \\ {a}_{-2} & =(-2)^{4}=16 \\ {a}_{-1} & =(-1)^{4}=1 \\ {a}_{0} & ={0}^{4}=0 \\ {a}_{1} & ={1}^{4}=1 \\ {a}_{2} & ={2}^{4}=16 \\ {a}_{3} & ={3}^{4}=81 \\  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set consists of the elements

$$
A={0,1,16,81…}.
$$

These are just the fourth powers including $0.$ Continuing the pattern, we have

$$
A={0,1,16,81,256,625,…}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Listing the Elements of a Set Defined Over a Special Set
questions.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined as

$$
A={\frac{1}{2}(-1)^{n}:n\in N}.
$$

Which of the following sets is equivalent to $A?$
questions.worked_solution:
The elements of $A$ are all the terms of the sequence ${a}_{n},$ given by

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{1}{2}(-1)^{n},\,n\in N={1,2,3,4,…}.
$$

Let's write down the first few terms of our sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(-1)^{1}=\frac{1}{2}(-1)=-\frac{1}{2} \\ {a}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(-1)^{2}=\frac{1}{2}(1)=\frac{1}{2} \\ {a}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(-1)^{3}=\frac{1}{2}(-1)=-\frac{1}{2} \\ {a}_{4} & =\frac{1}{2}(-1)^{4}=\frac{1}{2}(1)=\frac{1}{2} \\  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Our sequence alternates between $-\frac{1}{2}$ and $+\frac{1}{2}.$ Therefore, 

$$
A={-\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Listing the Elements of a Set Defined Over a Finite or Infinite Set
questions.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined as

$$
A={{n}^{2}+2n:n\in N,\,n\ge 2}.
$$

Which of the following sets is equivalent to $A?$
questions.worked_solution:
The condition after the "$:$" symbol

$$
n\in N,\,n\ge 2
$$

states that $n$ can be any natural number that satisfies the inequality $n\ge 2.$ In other words, 

$$
n={2,3,4,5,…}.
$$

Therefore, the elements of $A$ are all the terms of the sequence ${a}_{n},$ given by

$$
{a}_{n}={n}^{2}+2n,\,n\in {2,3,4,5,…}.
$$

Let's write down the first few terms of our sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{2} & ={2}^{2}+2(2)=4+4=8 \\ {a}_{3} & ={3}^{2}+2(3)=9+6=15 \\ {a}_{4} & ={4}^{2}+2(4)=16+8=24 \\ {a}_{5} & ={5}^{2}+2(5)=25+10=35 \\  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
A={8,15,24,35,…}.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the set $B,$ defined as

$$
B={\frac{1}{n+6}:n\in {\pm 1,\pm 2}}.
$$

Which of the following sets is equivalent to $B?$
questions.worked_solution:
The elements of $B$ are all the terms of the sequence ${b}_{n},$ given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{1}{n+6},\,n\in {-2,-1,1,2}.
$$

Let's write down all the terms of our sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} & =\frac{1}{(-2)+6}=\frac{1}{4} \\ {b}_{2} & =\frac{1}{(-1)+6}=\frac{1}{5} \\ {b}_{3} & =\frac{1}{1+6}=\frac{1}{7} \\ {b}_{4} & =\frac{1}{2+6}=\frac{1}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
B={\frac{1}{4},\frac{1}{5},\frac{1}{7},\frac{1}{8}}.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the set $B,$ defined as

$$
B={\frac{1}{2}(4)^{n}:n\in Z,\,-1\le n\le 2}.
$$

Which of the following sets is equivalent to $B?$
questions.worked_solution:
The condition after the "$:$" symbol

$$
n\in Z,\,-1\le n\le 2
$$

states that $n$ can be any integer number that satisfies the inequality $-1\le n\le 2.$ In other words, 

$$
n={-1,0,1,2}.
$$

Therefore, the elements of $B$ are all the terms of the sequence ${b}_{n},$ given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{1}{2}(4)^{n},\,n\in {-1,0,1,2}.
$$

Let's write down all the terms of our sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{-1} & =\frac{1}{2}(4)^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{8} \\ {b}_{0} & =\frac{1}{2}(4)^{0}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1=\frac{1}{2} \\ {b}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(4)^{1}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4=2 \\ {b}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(4)^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 16=8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
B={\frac{1}{8},\frac{1}{2},2,8}.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined as

$$
A={{a}_{n}\,:\,{a}_{n+1}=3{a}_{n}-4,\,{a}_{1}=0,\,n\in N}.
$$

Which of the following sets is equivalent to $A?$
questions.worked_solution:
The elements of $A$ are all the terms of the *recursive* sequence ${a}_{n},$ given by

$$
{a}_{n+1}=3{a}_{n}-4,\,{a}_{1}=0,\,n\in N.
$$

Let's write down the first few terms of our sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =0 \\ {a}_{2} & =3{a}_{1}-4 \\  & =3(0)-4 \\  & =-4 \\ {a}_{3} & =3{a}_{2}-4 \\  & =3(-4)-4 \\  & =-16 \\ {a}_{4} & =3{a}_{3}-4 \\  & =3(-16)-4 \\  & =-52 \\  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
A={0,-4,-16,-52,…}.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the set $B,$ defined as

$$
B={{b}_{n}\,:\,{b}_{n+1}={b}_{n}+5\,,\,{b}_{1}=2,\,n\in N}.
$$

Which of the following sets is equivalent to $B?$
questions.worked_solution:
The elements of $B$ are all the terms of the *recursive* sequence ${b}_{n},$ given by

$$
{b}_{n+1}={b}_{n}+5,\,{b}_{1}=2,\,n\in N.
$$

Let's write down the first few terms of our sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} & =2 \\ {b}_{2} & ={b}_{1}+5 \\  & =2+5 \\  & =7 \\ {b}_{3} & ={b}_{2}+5 \\  & =7+5 \\  & =12 \\ {b}_{4} & ={b}_{3}+5 \\  & =12+5 \\  & =17 \\  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
B={2,7,12,17,…}.
$$

$$
B={{b}_{n}\,:\,{b}_{n+1}=3{b}_{n}\,,\,{b}_{1}=2,\,n\in N}.

The elements of $B$ are all the terms of the *recursive* sequence ${b}_{n},$ given by

$$
{b}_{n+1}=3{b}_{n},\,{b}_{1}=2,\,n\in N.

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Listing the Elements of a Set Defined Over a Special Set
canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined as

$$
A = \{ (-1)^n \, n : n \in \mathbb{N} \}.
$$

Write down a set that's equivalent to $A$ using ellipsis notation.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The elements of $A$ are all the terms of the sequence $a_n,$ given by

$$
a_n = (-1)^n \,n, \qquad n \in \mathbb N = \{1,2,3,4,\ldots\}.
$$

Let's write down the first few terms of our sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =(-1)^{1}(1)=-1 \\ {a}_{2} & =(-1)^{2}(2)=2 \\ {a}_{3} & =(-1)^{3}(3)=-3 \\ {a}_{4} & =(-1)^{4}(4)=4 \\  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
A = \{ -1, 2, -3, 4,  \ldots \}.
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Listing the Elements of a Set Defined Over a Finite or Infinite Set
canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined as

$$
A = \left \{ 4^n : n \in \mathbb Z,\, -2\leq n\leq 2  \right \}.
$$

Describe $A$ by listing all of its elements.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The condition after the "$:$" symbol, 

$$
n \in \mathbb Z,\, -2\leq n\leq 2
$$

states that $n$ can be any integer that satisfies the inequality $-2\leq n\leq 2.$ 

Therefore, the elements of $A$ are all the terms of the sequence $a_n,$ given by

$$
a_n = 4^n, \qquad n \in \{0, \pm 1, \pm 2\}.
$$

Let's write down all the terms of our sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{-2} & ={4}^{-2}=\frac{1}{16} \\ {a}_{-1} & ={4}^{-1}=\frac{1}{4} \\ {a}_{0} & ={4}^{0}=1 \\ {a}_{1} & ={4}^{1}=4 \\ {a}_{2} & ={4}^{2}=16\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
A = \left\{\dfrac{1}{16},\,\dfrac{1}{4},\,1,\,4,\,16 \right\}.
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Listing the Elements of a Set Defined Using a Recursive Sequence
canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined as

$$
A = \big \{ a_n \,:\,a_{n+1} = 2a_{n} - 1, \, a_1 = 2,\, n \in \mathbb N \big\}.
$$

Write down a set that's equivalent to $A$ using ellipsis notation.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The elements of $A$ are all the terms of the *recursive* sequence $a_n,$ given by

$$
a_{n+1} =2a_{n} - 1, \quad a_1 =2,\qquad n \in \mathbb N.
$$

Let's write down the first few terms of our sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =2 \\ {a}_{2} & =2{a}_{1}-1 \\  & =2(2)-1 \\  & =3 \\ {a}_{3} & =2{a}_{2}-1 \\  & =2(3)-1 \\  & =5 \\ {a}_{4} & =2{a}_{3}-1 \\  & =2(5)-1 \\  & =9 \\ {a}_{5} & =2{a}_{4}-1 \\  & =2(9)-1 \\  & =17 \\  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
A = \left\{2,3,5,9,17,\ldots \right\}.
$$
